name: Qwik
tagline: A web framework that resumes serialized application state in the browser.
hook: Generates root instructions from .ruler sources and reserves hydration vocabulary for comparisons with other frameworks.
summary: Qwik generates its root guide from Ruler sources and keeps committed guidance separate from local skill copies. Six skills cover focused tasks, while the root file defines the language and checks used for resumability.

techniques.title: Keep shared guidance in a generator input
techniques.body: Root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are generated but committed, while tool-specific skill copies are regenerated locally. The file identifies .ruler as the editable source and describes a CI check for drift.
techniques.quote:
To change guidance, edit `.ruler/`, run `ruler apply`, and commit the regenerated root files
alongside your `.ruler/` change. Never hand-edit the generated files.

techniques.title: Route work to six source skills
techniques.body: A table maps core, router, optimizer, end-to-end testing, documentation, and guidance maintenance to named skills. If generated copies are absent, the guide gives the original .ruler path as the fallback.
techniques.quote:
If a skill above is not loadable, its copy has not been generated in this worktree yet — run the
`ruler apply` step from Setup, or read the source directly at `.ruler/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.

techniques.title: Define the vocabulary from the execution model
techniques.body: The guide explains that client execution resumes from serialized state rather than reconstructing it. It forbids hydration terminology for Qwik mechanisms while allowing the term when explicitly comparing other frameworks.
techniques.quote:
Never describe Qwik or any part of how Qwik works as hydration. Qwik does not hydrate. Qwik is
resumable: the server serializes application state and listeners into the HTML, and the client
resumes execution exactly where the server left off, without re-running component code or
rebuilding the framework state.

techniques.title: Check both sides of a protocol change
techniques.body: Test guidance distinguishes unit tests, optimizer fixtures, and browser-dependent behavior. Changes to serialization or loader protocols require writer and reader coverage rather than a test of only the edited side.
techniques.quote:
For serialization, hydration, streaming, or loader protocol changes, test both the writer and the
  reader path.

steal: Identify both the editable instruction source and its generated outputs.
Provide a source-path fallback when skill installation is missing.
Explain the technical distinction behind a vocabulary rule.
Require tests on both ends of a serialization or protocol change.
outline: Qwik v2 agents reference, instructions and rules
